summary:
I fixed both selected problems in m5-worker-transport.test.mjs, the only source file changed. The syntax check passed, and the one bounded controlled-group run passed 7 of 7 tests. The physical progress test was not run.

Starting file: 138,655 bytes, sha256 38f20142…. Result: 145,250 bytes, sha256 7c1e5e42621d01beaab830a687a863b6e447d4b0a9152d0ea16841b2a884f4a6.

(1) Completion timestamp (PHASE1-PROOF-001). A new function in the same file, m5ProgressTiming(captures, spawnedAt), replaces the old check that looked for "complete\n" inside a single callback. It joins the captured chunks in order. The completion time is the capture time at which the joined bytes first contain a whole, newline-terminated "complete" record. If no capture completes that record, the result is null; it never falls back to the owner's duration or a default time. The physical progress-lease test now uses this function. It keeps the same three timing fields and the same assertion that completion came after the initial lease. Spawn time, acknowledgements and byte checks are unchanged.

(2) Evidence when a controlled drive fails (PHASE1-PROOF-002). If the drive or one of its assertions throws, m5ControlledRun now saves the captures, acknowledgements, timeouts, signals, the log and the drive failure before rethrowing. It also records whether the owner is still pending or has settled, using a non-blocking check, so it never waits on an owner that cannot finish and never invents an exit, close or result. If saving the evidence itself fails, that is only logged as a diagnostic, and the identical original error is rethrown. The success path is unchanged.

Two new tests were added to the existing controlled real-owner group:
- **Completion timing:** 14 actual-owner runs with a 100 ms lease. The final record is delivered intact, coalesced with the previous record, coalesced and split, split at each of its 8 internal boundaries, and one byte per callback. Every one gives exactly 200 ms, with no timeouts and a success result. The test also checks that only the intact and coalesced runs carry the whole record in one callback, which is the condition that broke the old check. Missing and unterminated completion both give null.
- **Drive failure:** a deliberate contrary assertion fails after the real inactivity timeout and SIGTERM at 160 ms. The test confirms that the identical AssertionError comes back within one event-loop turn. The saved record holds the acknowledgement at 60 ms, the inactivity timeout and SIGTERM at 160 ms, an owner still pending, no exit or close, and no result.

Checks (pinned Node 24.7.0; its hash and the private-owner harness hash were verified first):
- **Syntax:** exit 0.
- **Controlled group:** run once with the exact `^M5 actual owner, controlled clock:` pattern, TAP output, concurrency 1, and a 60 s Python bound. It exited 0 in 0.647 s: 7 tests, 7 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled. It wrote 23 evidence files.

TMPDIR pointed into scratch, and the existing cleanup removed each run's temporary folder. Logs, evidence and the result records are in qualification-scratch/rc11-effect-phase1-01/native-03 (check-01/ and WORK_RESULT.json). No Git, build, package, observer or production changes were made. The earlier native-02 Run still stands as failed.
